KEN.note: No civil register or ID link stated.
Payments to government only; no e-procurement stated.
Convenience fee discussed; no consumer rule or redress body stated.

facts.fact: Treasury Cabinet Secretary John Mbadi told the Senate the e-Citizen platform stands at 16,000 services, up from 397, with payments made online through a single payment number.
Mbadi said e-Citizen processes about 120,000 transactions daily and collected Sh26.4 billion in the year to June 2023 and Sh100.8 billion in the year to June 2024.

KEN.note: No national ID system operation stated.
No register keyed on the ID number stated.

facts.fact: Mbadi said the e-Citizen system has been handed over to the government and is operated by the ICT Authority on a contractual basis, with a three-year contract after which the government will decide whether to continue.
Mbadi said the ICT Authority operates the e-Citizen platform that carries services of government bodies, collecting money for government and paying the service provider.

KEN.note: No survey of adults with accounts stated.
No mobile money service or switch stated.

facts.fact: Treasury Cabinet Secretary John Mbadi said government has collected at least Sh127.2 billion through the e-Citizen platform since the order to pay all government services through a single payment number.
Mbadi gave e-Citizen collections of Sh26.4 billion in the year to June 2023 and Sh100.8 billion in the year to June 2024.
